column1: # OCR-NEWSBENCH-2026-10-07: NewsBench (github.com/nealcaren/newsbench @ 2372b6b, MIT; 19 Library of Congress pages
# 1850s-1919, 15 scored, volunteer gold) scored with its own score.py (rapidfuzz 3.14.6), ocr-lab-round3's lab3-newsbench.
# Clone and readings live in $OCRLAB/newsbench (outside git). overall = 1-CER on lowercased alphanumerics (order-
# sensitive); bowF1 order-free; gap = bowF1 - overall (reading-order penalty). Measured by running code.
# apple-vision-wholepage: ops/truth/vision-read.swift (revision 3, accurate, language correction: the app's settings) on
# each whole JPG (2453-5975 px wide), one process per page, 1-8 s each. Vision scales the page down, so this is the
# floor, not the app's banded path.
# qwen3-vl-8b-4bit-whole: `--max-side 3300 --seconds 900`, max 12,000 tokens a page, 5,738 s of reading for 15 pages, peak
# footprint 9,432 MB; 2 pages cut at max_tokens (kept). The best local whole-page row on the broadsheets (0.863, just above
# the measured region rows' 0.847-0.856) but 0.678 on ordinary pages, where Qwen3.5-4B reads 0.915: the two are strong on
# opposite page types (aggregates only; per-page not compared). Measured 2026-10-08.
# qwen3.5-4b-4bit-whole: its fitted row (no prompt or size override; the model's own resize), max 12,000 tokens a
# page, 2,586 s of reading for 15 pages, peak footprint 5,960 MB; 2 pages cut at max_tokens (kept). The best measured
# row, by its own reading order (gap 0.074), but weak on the broadsheets (0.570), where regions win. Measured 2026-10-08.
# churro-3b-8bit-whole: `--churro --max-side 1600`, max 12,000 tokens a page, 4,811 s of reading for 15 pages, peak
# footprint 6,043 MB; 11 of 15 pages cut at max_tokens (kept). No better than Vision whole-page: the page at 1,600 px
# is too small for newsprint, and the token cap ends the rest. Measured 2026-10-08.
# churro-3b-8bit-yolo: `--churro --max-side 1600`, max 3000 tokens a region, 9,742 s of reading for 15 pages (~650 s a page), peak
# footprint 6,043 MB; 2 pages each have one region cut at max_tokens (kept, as bakeoff.sh keeps them). One earlier try of p.6
# (mss3413201323-27) died on a Metal GPU timeout after 2,306 s and was reread.
# region `yolo` rows: ops/ocrlab/newsbench.sh <reader> yolo — DocLayout-YOLO (ONNX, imgsz 1024) on each page, then
# dedupe-regions.py: 1,010 regions over the 15 pages, 11 s of detection in all. Read in the stand-in order (columns by
# x-centre), not a model's, which is why `overall` sits 0.20-0.24 under bowF1: the order costs more than the reader.
# layout-regions.py's ink_covered is not a coverage measure on these JPGs (0.028 on mss3413201628-41, whose region
# reads score bowF1 0.935 by Vision, 0.957 by PaddleOCR-VL; the page's ground is light, median 249). Cause not looked for: it changes nothing here.
# vision-yolo: vision-read.swift on the regions, 163 s for 15 pages, peak footprint 274 MB. paddleocr-vl-1.6-4bit-yolo: prompt `OCR:`,
# 604 s of reading for 15 pages, peak footprint 2,559 MB (both the guard's), no read cut.
# dots.mocr-4bit-yolo: its fitted prompt and `--max-side 2000`, max 3000 tokens a region, 1,654 s of reading for 15 pages,
# peak footprint 5,415 MB; one region on p.6 cut at max_tokens (kept).
# nara-qwen-3.5-2b-4bit-yolo (2026-10-08, lab3-extras): its prompt.txt and repetition penalty 1.1, max 3000 tokens a region,
# 1,306 s of reading for 15 pages, peak footprint 3,881 MB, no page reported cut.
# reference rows are the published scoresheet.md's, not run here.
